title: Behavioral and Transcriptional Effects of Short or Prolonged Fasting on the Memory Performances of Lymnaea stagnalis

nodes.label: Lymnaea stagnalis
nodes.description: Pond snail used as a model system to study fasting, learning, memory, and neuroplasticity.

nodes.label: Garcia effect
nodes.description: A learning paradigm in which a single pairing of an appetitive stimulus with a heat stressor produces a learned taste-specific negative hedonic shift.

nodes.label: Short-term fasting
nodes.description: Fasting for a short period, represented in this study by 1 day of food deprivation in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Prolonged fasting
nodes.description: Fasting for a prolonged period, represented in this study by 5 days of food deprivation in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Memory performance
nodes.description: Behavioral performance in the memory test based on the Garcia effect procedure.

nodes.label: Heat-shock stressor
nodes.description: A heat-shock procedure used as the nausea-inducing stimulus in the Garcia effect procedure.

nodes.label: Carrot slurry
nodes.description: Novel appetitive stimulus and food taste paired with the heat-shock stressor during the Garcia effect procedure.

nodes.label: Taste-specific negative hedonic shift
nodes.description: Learned reduction in the hedonic response to the paired taste following the Garcia effect procedure.

nodes.label: Visceral sickness
nodes.description: Nausea or visceral sickness described as necessary for acquisition of the Garcia effect in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Insulin
nodes.description: Hormone administered to severely fasting snails to investigate its role in memory performance and the insulin system.

nodes.label: Insulin receptor antibody
nodes.description: Antibody against the insulin receptor used as an antagonist to block insulin action in 1-day-fasting snails.

nodes.label: Insulin release spike
nodes.description: Increase in insulin release proposed to occur in the central nervous system during short-term fasting.

nodes.label: Neuroplasticity
nodes.description: Neural plasticity associated with the transcriptional and memory effects of fasting.

nodes.label: Energy homeostasis
nodes.description: Physiological energy regulation targeted in the transcriptional analyses of fasting effects.

nodes.label: Neuroplasticity-related gene upregulation
nodes.description: Upregulation of genes involved in neuroplasticity associated with short-term fasting in the study's interpretation.

nodes.label: Energy-homeostasis gene upregulation
nodes.description: Upregulation of genes involved in energy homeostasis and animal survival associated with long-term fasting.

nodes.label: Long-term memory formation
nodes.description: Formation of long-term memory following the Garcia effect procedure.

nodes.label: Memory expression
nodes.description: Behavioral expression of formed memory during testing after the Garcia effect procedure.

nodes.label: LymHSP70
nodes.description: Heat shock protein 70 target analyzed by gene expression methods; its heat-shock-induced upregulation was reported to play a necessary role in long-term memory formation after the Garcia effect.

nodes.label: LymMIPII
nodes.description: Molluscan insulin peptide II target analyzed for transcriptional changes associated with fasting and neuroplasticity.

nodes.label: LymMIPR
nodes.description: Molluscan insulin peptide receptor target analyzed for transcriptional changes associated with fasting and neuroplasticity.

nodes.label: LymGRIN1
nodes.description: Ionotropic glutamate receptor NMDA type subunit 1 target analyzed in relation to neuronal plasticity and memory.

nodes.label: LymCREB1
nodes.description: cAMP response element-binding protein 1 transcription factor target analyzed in relation to neuronal plasticity and memory.

nodes.label: LymNPY
nodes.description: Neuropeptide Y target involved in the study's analysis of hunger, energy balance, and neuroplasticity.

nodes.label: LymMEN1
nodes.description: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 target analyzed in relation to synapse formation, glucose metabolism, and the insulin pathway.

nodes.label: LymTPH
nodes.description: Tryptophan hydroxylase target analyzed as a rate-limiting enzyme for serotonin synthesis.

nodes.label: LymSERT
nodes.description: Serotonin transporter target analyzed as part of the serotonergic system.

nodes.label: Real-time PCR
nodes.description: Method used to analyze gene expression levels in the central nervous system and central ring ganglia of snails.

nodes.label: Gene expression
nodes.description: Transcriptional expression of selected targets measured in snail central nervous system tissues.

nodes.label: Lymnaea
nodes.description: Genus referenced in the study through L. stagnalis.

nodes.label: Yerkes-Dodson/Hebb law
nodes.description: Model invoked to explain how an optimal level of hunger-related stress can enhance memory whereas prolonged starvation prioritizes survival and energy homeostasis.

nodes.label: Learning
nodes.description: Behavioral learning studied in Lymnaea, including associative learning and food-deprivation-enhanced learning.

nodes.label: Conditioned taste aversion acquisition

nodes.label: Long-term synaptic plasticity
nodes.description: Long-term changes in synaptic function associated with insulin-like peptide and memory in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Food deprivation
nodes.description: Food deprivation examined as a state affecting learning in pond snails.

nodes.label: Insulin injection
nodes.description: Experimental insulin administration used to induce long-term memory in pond snails.

nodes.label: Shell damage
nodes.description: Damage to the shell of Lymnaea examined as a stimulus associated with enhanced memory formation.

nodes.label: Serotonin
nodes.description: Neurotransmitter studied in relation to feeding behavior and enhancement of long-term memory in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Predator detection
nodes.description: Detection of predators associated with enhancement of long-term memory in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Quercetin
nodes.description: Flavonoid reported to enhance long-term memory formation and configural learning memory in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Epicatechin
nodes.description: Flavonol present in cocoa reported to enhance snail memory.

nodes.label: MEN1 tumor suppressor gene
nodes.description: Tumor suppressor gene reported as required for long-term memory formation in an aversive operant conditioning model of Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Fasting activation of AgRP neurons

nodes.description: Receptors reported to be required for fasting activation of AgRP neurons and discussed in memory mechanisms.

nodes.description: Pond snail species in which conditioned taste aversion has been demonstrated.

nodes.label: Selective associability
nodes.description: The selective association of a particular novel taste with a specific negative event in conditioned taste aversion.

nodes.label: Latent inhibition
nodes.description: The reduced ability of a previously experienced, non-aversive taste to serve as the key taste for conditioned taste aversion.

nodes.label: Long-delay learning
nodes.description: Conditioned taste aversion learning that can occur despite a long interval between the conditioned stimulus and unconditioned stimulus.

nodes.label: Trace conditioning
nodes.description: Pavlovian conditioning in which a temporal gap occurs between termination of the conditioned stimulus and onset of the unconditioned stimulus.

nodes.label: Single-trial learning
nodes.description: Formation of conditioned taste aversion after a single pairing or trial, reported in mammals and demonstrated with some probability in snails.

nodes.label: Sucrose solution
nodes.description: Sweet solution used as the conditioned stimulus in the snail conditioned taste aversion paradigm and as a novel taste in mammalian studies.

nodes.label: KCl solution
nodes.description: Bitter, aversive solution used as the unconditioned stimulus in snail conditioned taste aversion experiments.

nodes.label: Sucrose–KCl pairing
nodes.description: Temporally contingent pairing of a sweet sucrose solution with an aversive KCl solution in snails.

nodes.label: Feeding response
nodes.description: Snail feeding behavior, including an increase in biting in response to sucrose.

nodes.label: Whole-body withdrawal response
nodes.description: Aversive withdrawal behavior induced by KCl solution in snails.

nodes.label: Feeding response suppression
nodes.description: Suppression of the feeding response after conditioned taste aversion training, so that sucrose no longer elicits feeding.

nodes.label: Glutamate
nodes.description: Neurotransmitter whose release was observed after LiCl injection and whose injection into the basolateral amygdala enhanced mammalian conditioned taste aversion.

nodes.label: De novo protein synthesis

The annotated checklist on the extant terrestrial mollusks from Hispaniola Island based on literature from 1758 to 2020 is here presented. We report 612 taxa distributed in three subclasses, 129 genera and 39 families. The most representative families are Annulariidae with 26 genera and 233 species, and Urocoptidae with 14 genera and 104, respectively. As more information is produced from the different families reported, these numbers can vary considerably.

To better predict population evolution of invasive species in introduced areas it is critical to identify and understand the mechanisms driving genetic diversity and structure in their native range. Here, we combined analyses of the mitochondrial COI gene and 11 microsatellite markers to investigate both past demographic history and contemporaneous genetic structure in the native area of the gastropod Tritia neritea , using Bayesian skyline plots (BSP), multivariate analyses and Bayesian clustering. The BSP framework revealed population expansions, dated after the last glacial maximum. The haplotype network revealed a strong geographic clustering. Multivariate analyses and Bayesian clustering highlighted the strong genetic structure at all scales, between the Black Sea and the Adriatic Sea, but also within basins. Within basins, a random pattern of genetic patchiness was observed, suggesting a superimposition of processes involving natural biological effects (no larval phase and thus limited larval dispersal) and putative anthropogenic transport of specimens. Contrary to the introduced area, no isolation-by-distance patterns were recovered in the Mediterranean or the Black Seas, highlighting different mechanisms at play on both native and introduced areas, triggering unknown consequences for species’ evolutionary trajectories. These results of Tritia neritea populations on its native range highlight a mixture of ancient and recent processes, with the effects of paleoclimates and life history traits likely tangled with the effects of human-mediated dispersal.

nodes.description: A muscular tongue-like feeding structure bearing chitinous teeth in gastropods.

nodes.label: invasive epiphytic algae

nodes.label: predator avoidance

nodes.label: Pomacea

nodes.label: Helisoma anceps

nodes.label: Gyraulus sp.

nodes.label: Parasite infective stages

nodes.label: Motility

title: Memory Trace in Feeding Neural Circuitry Underlying Conditioned Taste Aversion in Lymnaea

nodes.label: Lymnaea
nodes.description: Genus referenced in the species name Lymnaea stagnalis and in descriptions of the pond snail model.

nodes.label: Lymnaea stagnalis
nodes.description: Pond snail used to study conditioned taste aversion and feeding neural circuitry.

nodes.label: Conditioned taste aversion
nodes.description: Associative learning in which pairing sucrose with KCl causes the sucrose-conditioned feeding response to be reduced and retained as long-term memory.

nodes.label: Long-term memory
nodes.description: Persistent memory into which Lymnaea can consolidate conditioned taste aversion; the aversion persists for more than a month.

nodes.label: Taste aversion training
nodes.description: Training procedure involving repeated paired presentations of a sucrose conditioned stimulus and KCl unconditioned stimulus.

nodes.label: Conditioned stimulus (sucrose)
nodes.description: The appetitive sucrose stimulus applied to the snail lips during taste aversion training.

nodes.label: Unconditioned stimulus (KCl)
nodes.description: The aversive KCl stimulus paired with sucrose during taste aversion training.

nodes.label: Feeding response
nodes.description: Feeding behavior elicited by sucrose and measured by rasping or biting responses.

nodes.label: Feeding central pattern generator
nodes.description: Neural central pattern generator containing feeding interneurons including N1M and N3t cells.

nodes.label: Cerebral giant cell
nodes.description: Key regulatory neuron for the feeding CPG that receives associated chemosensory signals and activates the N3t cell.

nodes.label: Neuron 1 medial cell
nodes.description: Interneuron in the feeding CPG that is inhibited by the N3t cell.

nodes.label: Neuron 3 tonic cell
nodes.description: Feeding CPG interneuron that receives excitatory input from the CGC and tonically inhibits the N1M cell.

nodes.label: B1 motor neuron
nodes.description: Large motor neuron in which evoked EPSPs were recorded as a monitor of CGC-related synaptic input.

nodes.label: B3 motor neuron
nodes.description: Motor neuron in which spontaneous EPSPs were recorded as an indirect monitor of N3t input and neurotransmitter release.

nodes.label: CGC-N3t synaptic connection
nodes.description: Excitatory monosynaptic connection from the CGC to the N3t cell, monitored through evoked B1 motor-neuron EPSPs.

nodes.label: N3t-N1M synaptic connection
nodes.description: Inhibitory monosynaptic connection from the N3t cell to the N1M cell, whose facilitation is associated with taste aversion training.

nodes.label: B1 evoked EPSP
nodes.description: Evoked compound monosynaptic excitatory postsynaptic potential recorded in the B1 motor neuron after CGC activation; its amplitude did not differ among training groups.

nodes.label: B3 spontaneous EPSP
nodes.description: Spontaneous monosynaptic excitatory postsynaptic potential recorded in the B3 motor neuron; its amplitude was significantly larger after taste aversion training.

nodes.label: N3t neurotransmitter release
nodes.description: Amount of neurotransmitter released from the N3t cell, inferred from the amplitude of spontaneous B3 EPSPs and increased after taste aversion training.

nodes.label: Feeding system
nodes.description: Neural feeding system of Lymnaea stagnalis containing interneurons, motoneurons, and modulatory cells.

nodes.label: N1 interneurons
nodes.description: Cholinergic interneurons in the Lymnaea feeding system that make synapses with feeding motoneurons.

nodes.label: Feeding motoneurons
nodes.description: Motoneurons in the feeding system of Lymnaea stagnalis receiving cholinergic synapses from N1 interneurons.

nodes.label: Central pattern generator
nodes.description: Rhythm-generating circuit involved in control of the Lymnaea feeding system.

nodes.label: N2v cells
nodes.description: Glutamatergic interneurons identified as central pattern generator interneurons in the Lymnaea feeding system.

nodes.label: Serotonergic neurotransmission
nodes.description: Serotonergic signaling investigated in the Lymnaea feeding system and in relation to nitric oxide modulation.

nodes.label: Nitric oxide
nodes.description: Signaling molecule reported to modulate serotonergic neurotransmission.

nodes.label: Serotonin receptors
nodes.description: Multiple receptor subtypes investigated in the feeding circuit of a pond snail.

nodes.label: Associative learning
nodes.description: Learning process examined through cellular and behavioral studies in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Long-term associative memory
nodes.description: Long-term memory associated with delayed nonsynaptic neuronal plasticity in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Episodic rhythmic behavior
nodes.description: Rhythmic behavior for which loss of self-inhibition was described as a cellular mechanism.

nodes.label: Loss of self-inhibition
nodes.description: Cellular change described as a mechanism for episodic rhythmic behavior.

nodes.label: Tonic inhibition
nodes.description: Inhibitory process examined in associative reward conditioning in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: PKA
nodes.description: Molecule involved in PKA-dependent regulation of synaptic enhancement between a buccal motor neuron and its regulatory interneuron.

nodes.label: Synaptic enhancement
nodes.description: Enhancement of synaptic transmission studied in Lymnaea and linked to memory-related processes.

nodes.label: CREB
nodes.description: Transcription factor studied in identifiable neurons of the Lymnaea central nervous system and in relation to synaptic enhancement.

nodes.label: CREB1 isoforms
nodes.description: Isoforms whose learning-dependent gene expression and dimerization were investigated in molluscan neurons and living cells.

nodes.id: De novo CREB synthesis in a presynaptic neuron
nodes.label: De novo CREB synthesis in a presynaptic neuron
nodes.description: New CREB synthesis in a presynaptic neuron reported as required for memory-related synaptic enhancement.

nodes.label: Memory consolidation
nodes.description: Memory process in which synaptic enhancement was reported to be involved.

nodes.label: mRNA copy number
nodes.description: Exact copy numbers of particular mRNAs in a single cell, determined using quantitative real-time RT-PCR.

nodes.label: Quantitative real-time RT-PCR
nodes.description: Quantitative method used to determine exact copy numbers of particular mRNAs in a single cell.

nodes.label: Conditioned taste aversion
nodes.description: An associative taste-aversion response in Lymnaea in which a conditioned stimulus paired with an aversive stimulus no longer elicits feeding and the aversion persists as long-term memory.

nodes.label: Taste aversion training
nodes.description: Pairing sucrose as a conditioned stimulus with KCl as an unconditioned stimulus to establish conditioned taste aversion.

nodes.label: Long-term memory
nodes.description: A persistent memory state into which associative learning in Lymnaea can be consolidated.

nodes.label: Sucrose
nodes.description: An appetitive conditioned stimulus applied to the lips of Lymnaea during taste-aversion training.

nodes.label: KCl
nodes.description: An aversive unconditioned stimulus used in pairing with sucrose during taste-aversion training.

nodes.label: Feeding response
nodes.description: Feeding behavior elicited by an appetitive taste stimulus and suppressed after conditioned taste-aversion training.

nodes.label: Feeding central pattern generator
nodes.description: The neural circuit generating feeding activity in Lymnaea and containing N1M, N2, and N3t interneurons.

nodes.label: Cerebral giant cell
nodes.description: A key regulatory neuron for the feeding CPG that receives associated chemosensory inputs and activates downstream circuitry.

nodes.label: N1M cell
nodes.description: An interneuron of the Lymnaea feeding central pattern generator that is inhibited by N3t input.

nodes.label: N3t cell
nodes.description: A tonic interneuron in the feeding CPG that receives excitatory CGC input and inhibits the N1M cell through a monosynaptic connection.

nodes.label: B1 motor neuron
nodes.description: A large motor neuron receiving monosynaptic excitatory input from the CGC and used to monitor the CGC-to-N3t synaptic connection.

nodes.label: B3 motor neuron
nodes.description: A motor neuron receiving monosynaptic EPSPs from N3t and used to monitor N3t activity and neurotransmitter release.

nodes.label: Neurotransmitter release from N3t cell
nodes.description: Release of neurotransmitter from the N3t cell, inferred from the amplitude of spontaneous B3 EPSPs and increased after taste-aversion training.

nodes.label: Memory trace in feeding neural circuitry
nodes.description: The training-associated increase in spontaneous B3 EPSP amplitude interpreted as a memory trace involving enhanced neurotransmitter release from N3t.

nodes.label: CGC-N3t synaptic connection
nodes.description: The excitatory monosynaptic connection from the cerebral giant cell to the N3t cell, monitored through B1 EPSPs.

nodes.label: Associative learning
nodes.description: Learning involving associations, including associative reward conditioning and conditioned taste aversion in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Central pattern generator
nodes.description: A neuronal circuit involved in rhythm generation and feeding behavior in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Feeding system
nodes.description: The neuronal feeding system or feeding circuit of Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Serotonergic neurotransmission
nodes.description: Serotonin-mediated neurotransmission in the feeding circuit of a pond snail.

nodes.label: Nitric oxide
nodes.description: Nitric oxide investigated as a modulator of serotonergic neurotransmission.

nodes.label: Synaptic enhancement
nodes.description: Enhancement of synaptic transmission, including enhancement involved in memory consolidation.

nodes.label: CREB
nodes.description: A transcription-related neuronal factor studied in Lymnaea stagnalis, including its expression and function in learning and memory.

nodes.label: De novo CREB synthesis
nodes.description: New synthesis of CREB in a presynaptic neuron.

nodes.label: Memory consolidation
nodes.description: A memory-related process involving synaptic enhancement in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: PKA-dependent synaptic regulation
nodes.description: Protein kinase A-dependent regulation of synaptic enhancement between neurons in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Tonic inhibition
nodes.description: Persistent inhibitory neural activity studied in associative reward conditioning in Lymnaea.

nodes.label: Taste discrimination
nodes.description: Discrimination of tastes during conditioned taste aversion in Lymnaea stagnalis.

title: In Vitro Odor-Aversion Conditioning in a Terrestrial Mollusk

nodes.label: Limax marginatus
nodes.description: Laboratory-bred terrestrial slug species used in the experiments.

nodes.label: Limax
nodes.description: Terrestrial mollusk taxon discussed as having odor-learning and odor-aversion behaviors.

nodes.label: Odor-aversion conditioning
nodes.description: Differential conditioning in which an odor is paired with an aversive unconditioned stimulus to produce odor-avoidance responses.

nodes.label: In vitro odor-aversion conditioning system
nodes.description: Experimental in vitro system using isolated Limax brains containing the nose and motor output to study odor learning and aversion.

nodes.label: Isolated brain preparation
nodes.description: Whole-brain preparation containing the nose, sensory organs, and parietal nerves for in vitro conditioning and recording.

nodes.label: Odor learning
nodes.description: Ability of isolated Limax brain preparations to acquire odor-aversion responses after conditioning.

nodes.label: Aversively conditioned odors
nodes.description: Natively attractive odors that were paired with an aversive electrical stimulus and subsequently elicited avoidance-related responses.

nodes.label: Innately aversive odors
nodes.description: Odors that elicited avoidance-related responses in naive, nonconditioned preparations.

nodes.label: Natively attractive odors
nodes.description: Odors described as attractive to Limax before conditioning, including carrot, cucumber, potato, and rat chow odors.

nodes.label: Carrot odor
nodes.description: Natural odorant used as a conditioned stimulus and described as natively attractive to Limax.

nodes.label: Cucumber odor
nodes.description: Natural odorant used as a conditioned stimulus and described as natively attractive to Limax.

nodes.label: Onion odor
nodes.description: Natively aversive odor applied to naive preparations.

nodes.label: Garlic odor
nodes.description: Natively aversive odor applied to naive preparations.

nodes.label: Potato odor
nodes.description: Natively attractive odor applied to naive preparations for comparison with onion odor.

nodes.label: Rat chow odor
nodes.description: Natively attractive odor applied to naive preparations for comparison with garlic odor.

nodes.label: Electrical stimulation
nodes.description: Electrical stimulation of the external lip and anterior pedal nerves used as the unconditioned stimulus during in vitro conditioning.

nodes.label: External lip nerve
nodes.description: Afferent nerve electrically stimulated as part of the unconditioned stimulus.

nodes.label: Anterior pedal nerve
nodes.description: Afferent nerve electrically stimulated as part of the unconditioned stimulus.

nodes.label: Procerebrum
nodes.description: The olfactory central nervous system of Limax, abbreviated PC, containing ongoing network oscillations.

nodes.label: PC network oscillation
nodes.description: Synchronized ongoing neural oscillation in the Limax procerebrum, observable in vitro and modulated by odors.

nodes.label: PC network oscillation frequency
nodes.description: Frequency of the procerebrum network oscillation, which increased in response to aversively conditioned and innately aversive odors.

nodes.label: Parietal nerves
nodes.description: Nerves projecting to or connecting with the mantle muscle and used to observe motor-output discharges.

nodes.label: Parietal nerve discharges
nodes.description: Large-amplitude discharges in parietal nerves elicited by aversively conditioned odors in vitro.

nodes.label: Posterior visceral neuron
nodes.description: Motoneuron whose spikes were recorded from the left parietal nerves and used to quantify conditioned responses.

nodes.label: p-VN spikes
nodes.description: Spiking activity of the posterior visceral neuron used as an in vitro index of odor-induced avoidance behavior.

nodes.label: Avoidance behavior
nodes.description: Withdrawal or escape response elicited by aversively conditioned or innately aversive odors.

nodes.label: Mantle muscle shortening
nodes.description: Shortening of the mantle muscle observed during odor-induced withdrawal behavior.

nodes.label: Extracellular recording
nodes.description: Electrophysiological method used to record parietal nerve discharges and p-VN spikes.

nodes.label: Local field potential recording
nodes.description: Recording method used to measure local field potential oscillations in the procerebrum.

nodes.label: PC
nodes.description: Neural olfactory center referred to as PC, in which network oscillations are studied.

nodes.label: PC oscillation frequency
nodes.description: Frequency of oscillation in the PC network, whose pharmacological increase was reported to alter p-CSC firing.

nodes.label: Posterior cerebral serotonergic cell
nodes.description: Identifiable serotonergic neuron reported to discharge serotonin in the tentacle ganglion.

nodes.label: p-CSC discharges
nodes.description: Discharges of the posterior cerebral serotonergic cell.

nodes.label: Serotonin
nodes.description: Neurotransmitter released in the tentacle ganglion and reported to suppress aversive odor-induced p-VN discharges.

nodes.id: Serotonin release in the tentacle ganglion
nodes.label: Serotonin release in the tentacle ganglion
nodes.description: Release of serotonin in the tentacle ganglion following p-CSC discharges.

nodes.label: Tentacle ganglion
nodes.description: Ganglion in which p-CSC discharges release serotonin.

nodes.label: p-VN discharges
nodes.description: Discharges in the p-VN, including discharges induced by aversive odors.

nodes.label: p-CSC firing rate
nodes.description: Firing rate of the posterior cerebral serotonergic cell, reported to decrease when PC oscillation frequency was increased by acetylcholine.

nodes.label: Acetylcholine
nodes.description: Cholinergic agent used to increase PC oscillation frequency in preliminary pharmacological studies.

nodes.label: Odor discrimination
nodes.description: Olfactory processing involving discrimination between odors, including closely related odors and aversive versus attractive odors.

nodes.label: Odor-guided avoidance behavior
nodes.description: Avoidance behavior whose neural mechanism is proposed to involve PC oscillation frequency.

(Helicidae) along the Belgian coastal dunes Cepaea nemoralis (Linne) from Newport, Rhode Island Statistics on a colony of Cepaea nemoralis A mixed colony of Cepaea nemoralis and Cepaea hortensis on Long Island, New York Area effects in Cepaea The snails Cepaea nemoralis and C. hortensis are remarkable for an extensive and stable polymorphism involving the colour and banding of the shell. It was formerly thought that the variation in frequency of the different morphs between populations was random. Cain & Sheppard, for nemoralis and Clarke, for C. hortensis, have shown that in many English colonies visual selection by thrushes, and no doubt other predators, strongly influences the frequencies of the morphs, the more conspicuous on a given background being more heavily predated. In consequence populations tend to match their backgrounds, but remain polymorphic. In some districts of high chalk downland, this correspondence with background does not occur. The predominance of a few morphs irrespective of habitat and background characterizes areas vastly larger than that of a panmictic population. Such a constancy of morph frequencies over a large and diverse area in spite of visual selection we call an area effect. The principal district we have studied is the Marlborough Downs, where in an area of several square kilometres there are no five-banded C. nemoralis although in a contiguous area they predominate. Part of the non-five-banded area has a vast excess of browns, and another part of yellows. The form spread-banded and the cross-product ratio of pink and yellow to unbanded and banded also show such effects. In some places the morph frequencies change with extraordinary abruptness over 100 to 300 m. The area effects are not due to differential incidence of visual predation, nor, since they bear no relation to variation of habitat, to differences in its direction. In only two subareas do we think that visual selection is affecting morph frequencies. The observed frequency distributions cannot be accounted for by sampling drift (‘genetic drift’) at the present day since the numbers involved are far too large and the frequencies too constant over large areas. In the few populations that have been observed for up to 10 years, no major changes of frequency have been found. The probability of a reduction to a few isolated populations because of ploughing up or drought in the last 200 years and subsequent drift and expansion is shown by the known agricultural history of the district to be slight. Restriction by spread of C. hortensis is also unlikely. A few colonies with restricted variation which might seem to show the action of drift or the founder effect are only extreme examples of local tendencies. Moreover, subfossil material from just off the south-western corner of the district strongly suggests that the area effects seen there have been in existence since Neolithic times. A survey of another district of high downland (Lambourn Downs) has shown a similar state of affairs to that on the Marlborough Downs, with a large area characterized by excess of yellow and mid-banded, and adjacent to it localities in which visual selection is effective. Observations from various other places on and off the Chalk also indicate that area effects are frequent on the Chalk, but that away from it visual selection is the principal agent determining local variation in gene frequencies. nodes.label: Conditioned taste aversion
nodes.description: An associative learning phenomenon in which a conditioned stimulus such as sucrose is paired with an aversive stimulus such as KCl, reducing the subsequent feeding response.

nodes.description: Long-term memory formed following conditioned taste aversion training in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Food deprivation
nodes.description: Experimental deprivation of food for defined durations, including 1-day and 5-day deprivation, affecting conditioned taste aversion learning and memory recall.

nodes.label: Insulin injection
nodes.description: Injection of insulin into Lymnaea stagnalis, used to mimic aspects of the internal state associated with food deprivation before memory testing.

nodes.description: Insulin used experimentally to alter memory recall and hemolymph glucose concentration in Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Molluscan insulin-related peptide II
nodes.description: Molluscan insulin-related peptide II whose CNS mRNA expression was higher in day 13 good learners than in day 12 snails and day 13 poor learners.

nodes.description: Glucose concentration in snail hemolymph, which was decreased by insulin injection.

nodes.description: Receptor mediating insulin-related signaling; an anti-insulin receptor antibody was used to block insulin-receptor binding.

nodes.label: Anti-insulin receptor antibody
nodes.description: Antibody used to block binding between insulin and insulin receptors, preventing insulin-associated memory recall when co-injected with insulin.

nodes.label: Long-term memory recall
nodes.description: Behavioral retrieval of conditioned taste aversion long-term memory during post-test sessions.

nodes.description: Partially purified MIPs administered to snails; they decreased hemolymph glucose concentration in several feeding/deprivation states.

nodes.description: An inbred laboratory strain of Lymnaea stagnalis maintained under standardized temperatures for generations.

nodes.description: A freshly collected strain of Lymnaea stagnalis obtained from Stony Lake and exposed to naturally varying temperatures.

nodes.label: Heat shock
nodes.description: Exposure of snails to 30 °C artificial pond water for 1 h.

nodes.label: Garcia effect
nodes.description: A learned, taste-specific aversion produced when a novel taste is followed by heat shock in W-strain Lymnaea stagnalis.

nodes.label: Lymnaea stagnalis HSP70
nodes.description: Heat shock protein 70 transcript measured in Lymnaea stagnalis central ring ganglia.

nodes.label: Lymnaea stagnalis HSP40
nodes.description: Heat shock protein 40 transcript measured in Lymnaea stagnalis central ring ganglia.

nodes.label: GRIN1
nodes.description: Glutamate ionotropic receptor NMDA type subunit 1 transcript examined as a neuroplasticity-related target.

nodes.label: CREB1
nodes.description: cAMP response element-binding protein 1 transcript examined as a neuroplasticity-related target.

nodes.label: Common garden experimental design
nodes.description: An experimental design in which freshly collected and laboratory-inbred snails were housed under the same standardized conditions before comparison.

nodes.label: Thermal tolerance
nodes.description: The capacity to tolerate elevated temperature; the paper discusses this as potentially associated with higher basal HSP mRNA levels in Stony-strain snails.

nodes.label: Garcia-like effect
nodes.description: A learned aversion to a novel food stimulus after exposure to heat stress; in the W-strain, rasping in carrot slurry was reduced after the heat stress.

nodes.label: Garcia-effect training procedure
nodes.description: A behavioural procedure in which exposure to a novel food is followed by heat stress and subsequent measurement of feeding behaviour and molecular responses.

nodes.label: Heat stress
nodes.description: Heat-shock treatment used after exposure to a novel carrot-slurry stimulus; in W-strain snails it reduced subsequent rasping and upregulated several genes.

nodes.label: HSPs
nodes.description: Heat-shock proteins whose expression is upregulated by the behavioural procedure in W-strain snails and whose basal mRNA levels are higher in the Stony strain.

nodes.label: HSP70
nodes.description: A heat-shock protein gene or protein measured as a major physiological marker of heat stress; its basal mRNA level is higher in Stony-strain snails and its expression is upregulated by the procedure in W-strain snails.

nodes.label: HSP40
nodes.description: A heat-shock protein gene or protein whose basal mRNA level is higher in Stony-strain snails and whose expression is upregulated by the procedure in W-strain snails.

nodes.label: Heat tolerance
nodes.description: The heat-tolerance phenotype compared between snail strains experiencing different thermal environments; the Garcia-effect learning procedure was used as a measure of heat tolerance and HSP induction.

nodes.label: Long-term memory formation
nodes.description: A memory-related process associated in the text with GRIN1 and CREB1 upregulation in W-strain snails; the text reports correlation rather than demonstrating causation.

nodes.label: Predator detection
nodes.description: A behavioural mechanism differing between predator-experienced and predator-naive Lymnaea populations and correlated with the presence or absence of crayfish predators.

nodes.label: Crayfish predators
nodes.description: Predators whose presence or absence in adjacent lakes correlated with differences in predator detection among freshly collected Lymnaea strains.
